title: observability-pipeline-debug-notes-amelia-wip
content:
High-level summary:
- Incident window: 2026-02-27 ~17:00-18:30 UTC. Sudden drop (~75-90%) in tracing spans and metrics for inference-proxy and router components. Logs ingestion showed increased error rates and backpressure on the ingestion path.

What I observed (initial):
- Grafana: traces-per-minute for inference-proxy went from ~18k to ~3k at 17:05 UTC. Metrics ingestion (prometheus-push pipeline) for same services reported near-zero points for the same window.
- Alerting: Multiple "traces missing" alerts fired from SLO monitors and an internal pipeline "ingest-failure" alert.
- OTEL collector (hosted as DaemonSet in observability namespace) started throwing producer/kafka errors around 17:03 UTC.

Commands I ran / outputs (snippets):
- kubectl (checked collector logs):
  kubectl -n observability logs deploy/otel-collector -c otel-collector --since=2h | head -n 120
  -> repeated: ERROR otelcol/exporter/kafka: failed to publish batch: produce error: expired: write tcp 10.0.3.12:52344->10.0.1.5:9092: write: connection reset by peer

- Checked kafka consumer groups and lag:
  kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-1:9092 --describe --group metrics-ingest-consumer
  -> GROUP            TOPIC                        PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG  CONSUMER-ID
     metrics-ingest  metrics.inference-proxy        6          124530          124530           0   consumer-1
     metrics-ingest  metrics.inference-proxy        7          124128          124530         402   consumer-1
  -> Some partitions had small lag but several showed consumer side restarts (consumer-id changed frequently).

- Checked broker health:
  kubectl -n infra logs statefulset/kafka --tail=200
  -> Broker GC and network short writes around 17:02-17:06: "WARN [Producer IO thread to broker-3] Connection to node -1 could not be established" and "OutOfOrderSequenceException" in a couple of logs.

- Quick curl to internal ingestion API (to test fallback path):
  curl -v -X POST https://ingest.internal.redwood/v1/traces -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @sample-span.json
  -> 502 Bad Gateway from ingress-nginx (upstream prematurely closed connection).

- Checked node resources where otel collector runs:
  kubectl top pod -n observability | grep otel-collector
  -> CPU/Memory within normal range for most pods; one worker node showed transient disk pressure events around 16:58 UTC (kubelet eviction-pressure).

Error snippets I collected:
- "failed to publish batch: produce error: expired: write tcp ... write: connection reset by peer"
- "Broker responded with NotLeaderForPartition" (intermittent)
- "ingress-nginx upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream"

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kafka broker cluster had a transient leader shuffle / network partition between brokers causing producers to fail and OTEL collector producers to drop messages. Evidence: broker logs with leader/no-leader errors + producer connection resets.
2) Consumer side (metrics-ingest consumer) flapping / OOMing causing backlog and implicit backpressure upstream (collectors slowed/retried). Evidence: consumer-id rotated; consumer pod restarts in the same window in k8s events.
3) Storage/disk pressure on one or more nodes (kubelet eviction) caused collectors/ingress to restart or drop connections. Evidence: disk pressure event at 16:58 on a worker hosting ingress/collector.
4) Ingress (nginx) misconfiguration or burst of large traces causing timeout 502s. Evidence: ingress 502 messages for curl test.

Things I tried and immediate outcomes:
- Rotated OTEL collector to use alternate Kafka bootstrap list (kafka-2,kafka-3) temporarily: collectors shifted but still hit producer timeouts. Suggests problem not single-broker-only.
- Increased producer retries and linger.ms to batch more -> decreased error rate but latency increased; traces still lost for the 17:00 window (expected).
- Redeployed metrics-ingest-consumer with more memory (x2) and restart to clear potential OOM cycle -> consumer stayed up, lag reduced over ~20 minutes.
- Scaled up kafka brokers from 3->4 (quick k8s scale) to spread leadership -> broker logs stabilized after ~12 min and producer errors subsided.

Short-term mitigations applied:
- Increased OTEL collector producer retries and enabled async buffering for 1h during the incident window.
- Scaled metrics-ingest-consumer to 3 replicas to reduce partition rebalancing impact.
- Added temporary alert to detect "producer expired" error spikes in collector logs.

Observed result after mitigations:
- Spans/metrics recovery started ~17:40 UTC after brokers stabilized and consumers resumed steady processing. Partial data restored from buffered OTEL collector but some spans permanently lost (no local durable buffer configured).

Longer-term follow-ups / action items (open):
- Investigate broker-side root cause: correlate broker GC/pause windows with leader re-election events. Assigned to Ravi. (jira:OBS-1122)
- Add local persistent buffer to OTEL collector (disk-based queue) to avoid best-effort drops on transient broker failures. Evaluate otelcol file_queue or durable exporter option. Owner: me. Target: 2 weeks.
- Improve consumer liveness: add pod disruption budgets and set resource requests/limits to avoid OOM-induced rebalances. Owner: Lina.
- Harden ingress timeout handling for large trace batches; ensure 504/502s from ingress degrade gracefully and fall back to direct ingestion route. Owner: infra network team.
- Add a synthetic trace/metrics canary that exercises end-to-end ingest path every 60s (trace + metric point) with alerting on missing samples for >2 intervals. Owner: SRE.
- Postmortem draft: need to collect full broker logs, collector configs (current exporter settings), consumer GC logs, node eviction events.

Notes / questions to triage later:
- Do we have any durable storage/retry knobs on the collector right now? I think we have only in-memory queues for batching (small). Need to confirm exact exporter config in helm values.
- Should we consider using a managed kafka (confluent) for higher availability, or can we improve our operator config?
- Are there any retention/compaction policies that could interfere with consumers during leader re-election?

Timestamps & quick timeline (UTC):
- 16:55: normal traffic
- 17:02: first producer timeouts in otel-collector logs
- 17:03: alerts fired (ingest-failure, traces-missing)
- 17:05-17:25: highest error window; several consumer restarts observed
- 17:30: scaling and broker stabilization steps completed (partial)
- 17:40: trend shows recover to ~80% of previous levels

Raw snippets to paste into postmortem (sanitized):
- otel-collector.log: "ERROR exporter/kafka: failed to publish: produce error: expired: write tcp 10.0.3.12:52344->10.0.1.6:9092: write: connection reset by peer"
- kafka-broker.log: "WARN [ReplicaFetcherThread] NotLeaderForPartition: Partition 12 of topic metrics.inference-proxy has no leader for 12s"

Next immediate steps I will take (today):
- Collect and upload all otel-collector deployment YAMLs and helm values to the postmortem draft page (confluence:OBS-2843).
- Pull full kafka broker logs for the 16:45-18:00 window and hand off to Ravi.
- Add short-term durable buffering to one collector (test) and run soak for 48h to validate behavior.

If anyone else is debugging this, useful quick checks:
- kubectl get events -n observability --sort-by=.lastTimestamp (watch for OOM/kubelet eviction)
- kubectl -n observability logs deploy/otel-collector -c otel-collector --since=3h | grep -E "expired|NotLeaderForPartition|connection reset"
- kafka-consumer-groups --describe --bootstrap-server kafka-1:9092 --group metrics-ingest
- curl -v to internal ingestion endpoint to reproduce ingress 502/504

-- Amelia
